photoSkips.why: reviewed: a fish, not the aquarium

photoSkips.name: Perelman Theater
photoSkips.why: reviewed: Kimmel Center exterior, not the theater inside

sample.name: Walter K Gordon Theater
facts: A 650-seat proscenium theater with an unobstructed view from every seat.
The hub of the performing arts at Rutgers-Camden.
Run by Rutgers University–Camden

sample.name: Iron Gate Theater
facts: Built in 1886 and designed by architect Theophilus Parsons Chandler.
Located in a national historic landmark building that also houses the Tabernacle Church and the Christian Association.
The former church sanctuary was converted to a theater without altering the interior.

sample.name: Philadelphia Shakespeare Theatre
facts: Founded in 1989 as the Red Heel Theatre.
Changed its name and purpose in 1993.
Address: 2111 Sansom Street, Philadelphia

sample.name: Regal UA Main Street Theatre
facts: Part of the Regal Cinemas chain
Address: 3720 Main Street, Philadelphia

sample.name: Prince Music Theatre
facts: Bought by the Philadelphia Film Society in March 2015 and renamed Prince Theater.
Now operated by the Film Society as the Film Society Center.
Opened in 1921

sample.name: Forrest Theatre
facts: Named for the 19th century actor Edwin Forrest, who was born in Philadelphia.
Opened with a performance of The Red Robe.
Opened in 1928

sample.name: Adventure Aquarium
facts: Formerly the Thomas H. Kean New Jersey State Aquarium.
Reopened in its current form on May 25, 2005.
Home to about 8,000 animals in freshwater, marine and semi-aquatic habitats.

sample.name: ComedySportz
facts: Performs at The Adrienne Theater in the Rittenhouse section of Center City.
Flagship show is ComedySportz, a competitive improv comedy match.
Address: 2030 Sansom Street, Philadelphia

sample.name: Kurtz Performing Arts Center
facts: Opened in January 2010 at William Penn Charter School.
A LEED Gold certified building with a green roof.
Named by the Kurtz family in memory of David L. Kurtz.

sample.name: Cinemark University City Penn 6
facts: Has six screens and 1,179 seats.
Cinemark took over the theater in June 2013.
Part of the Cinemark chain

sample.name: Venice Island Performing Arts and Recreational Facility
facts: Opened with a celebration of live music and art in October 2014.
The transformation received a 2015 Groundbreaker Award.
Address: 7 Lock Street, Philadelphia

sample.name: PFS Bourse Theater
facts: Opened in 1990 as the Ritz at the Bourse.
Philadelphia Film Society took over operation in 2021 and renovated all five theaters.
Has 5 screens

sample.name: Miller Theater
facts: Originally the Sam S. Shubert Theatre, built by the Shubert brothers in 1918 to honor their late brother Sam.
Formerly the Merriam Theater, it was purchased by the Kimmel Center in November 2016.
Renamed for Alan B. Miller, a founding board member of the Kimmel Center.

sample.name: Punch Line Philly
facts: Comedy club in Fishtown with about 300 seats, booked by Live Nation's House of Blues Entertainment division.
Has a lobby bar serving craft beers and pub grub, plus an outdoor patio.
Hosts local talent showcases and burlesque shows.

sample.name: Irvine Auditorium
facts: Opened in May 1929 and built between 1926 and 1932.
Houses the Curtis Organ, nearly 11,000 pipes, built for the 1926 Sesquicentennial Exposition and donated in 1928.
Restored and renovated in 1997 to 2000 by Venturi, Scott Brown & Associates.

sample.name: AMC Broadstreet 7
facts: Opened December 5, 2006 as the Pearl Theatre at Avenue North, next to Temple University.
Named for the former Pearl Theatre on Ridge Avenue and in memory of entertainer Pearl Bailey.
AMC took over management in September 2016.

sample.name: Ritz Five
facts: Founded by Ramon L. Posel as a three-screen theatre in 1976 and expanded to five screens in 1985.
Premiered M. Night Shyamalan's debut feature Praying with Anger in 1992.
Ownership transferred to Landmark Theatres in March 2007.

sample.name: Fringe Arts
facts: Address: 140 North Christopher Columbus Boulevard, Philadelphia

sample.name: Lantern Theater Company
facts: Run by Lantern Theater Company
Also known as St. Stephen's Theater
Address: 923 Ludlow Street, Philadelphia

sample.name: Bushfire Theatre of Performing Arts
facts: Founded in 1977 by Alfred Simpkins as an African-American professional theatre company.
Housed in the old Locust Street Theater, a former vaudeville house turned movie house.
The 428-seat space on 52nd Street is home to its resident ensemble.

sample.name: Theatre of Living Arts
facts: The building dates to the early 1900s as a nickelodeon.
Became a regional theater led by Andre Gregory in the 1960s, named Theatre of the Living Arts.
The Philadelphia Council for the Performing Arts acquired the derelict cinema in 1964.

sample.name: Walnut Street Theatre
facts: Founded in 1808 and the oldest operating theatre in the United States.
Was the first theatre to install gas footlights, in 1837.
Hosted the first presidential debate between Gerald Ford and Jimmy Carter on September 23, 1976.

sample.name: F. M. Kirby Auditorium
facts: Located inside the National Constitution Center at 525 Arch Street.
Has a permanent stage and a capacity of 209 guests.
Run by National Constitution Center

sample.name: Suzanne Roberts Theatre
facts: Seats 365 people.
Named for Suzanne Roberts, an actress, playwright and director who hosted the TV program Seeking Solutions.
Her husband, Ralph J. Roberts, founded Comcast.
